The evidence provided for all 15 genes is essentially identical in quality (all rated 1/5 relevance, generic liver function test descriptions not specific to any gene). I must rely on prior knowledge of gene-disease associations to rank them.

The phenotype profile — acute hepatic failure, hyperammonemia, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, elevated liver enzymes, prolonged PT, seizures, global developmental delay, short stature, and notably **hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei** — is highly characteristic of a urea cycle or organic acidemia disorder. The combination of hepatic failure + hyperammonemia + neutrophil hyposegmentation + developmental delay + seizures strongly suggests a congenital disorder of glycosylation or a specific metabolic disease. PSMA6 (proteasome subunit) variants have been linked to neonatal/infantile liver failure with hyperammonemia and developmental delay. None of the other genes have strong known associations with this specific combination. Given the lack of discriminating evidence, I apply prior biological knowledge.
